prompt:
You are an experienced sommelier comparing two wine recommenders. A
customer with no wine knowledge made this request:

"Hi, I am looking to try something new and want a light red wine that is a little sweet and tastes like flowers and mushrooms."

List A:
Wine 1: Cabernet Sauvignon, US, $11. Tasting note: "Good red wine in a light, herbaceous style. Tastes fresh and clean as if it was made with good quality standards. Lacks much Cabernet character, however, but adds sufficient cherry and berry flavors to make it complete."
Wine 2: Merlot, US, $15. Tasting note: "This is a beautiful red wine to drink now for its rich, ripe flavors and overall balance. It's soft in acids and fine in tannins, offering heady waves of black cherries, currants and chocolate. Easy to find, with nearly 75,000 cases produced."
Wine 3: Red Blend, US, $17. Tasting note: "This light- to medium-bodied red wine doesn't take itself too seriously and will be versatile with food. The fruity, almost jammy and fresh aromas lead to dry, substantive flavors and a tempting, smooth texture."
Wine 4: Primitivo, US, $28. Tasting note: "Sweet, but not very, and lacks the rich opulence you want in a dessert red wine. Shows plenty of raspberry and cherry flavor, but would benefit from greater intensity and sweetness."
Wine 5: Cabernet Sauvignon, US, $25. Tasting note: "An okay red wine. It's soft, dry and common in structure, with thin flavors of blackberries, spices and a touch of oak."

List B:
Wine 1: Pinot Noir, US, $19. Tasting note: "This quirky medium-bodied wine has a flavor spectrum all its own. It smells floral and tastes like spiced red candy, and is noticeably sweet."
Wine 2: Pinot Noir, US, $60. Tasting note: "This graceful, light-bodied wine from a promising new brand smells of strawberries and cream and tastes fresh and well-balanced. Red cherry, strawberry and clove notes blend with the creamy texture, leaving a soft but lightly tannic feel on the tongue that makes the wine even more appetizing and complete."
Wine 3: Bordeaux-style Red Blend, France, $11. Tasting note: "In a light, fresh style, this is an attractive red berry fruited wine. There are light tannins, soft strawberry flavors and a light acidity."
Wine 4: Bordeaux-style Red Blend, France, $15. Tasting note: "The wine feels light and very soft. There are some attractive red berry fruits, along with acidity and wood flavors, but the tannic structure is hardly there. It's an enjoyable, lightweight wine to drink now through 2016."
Wine 5: Bordeaux-style Red Blend, France, $25. Tasting note: "Light, fruity and fragrant, this is an attractive, crisp wine that highlights red-berry fruits and soft acidity. It's a wine to drink now."

Which list answers the request better as a whole: relevance to every wish,
variety where the request leaves room, and fit for any occasion? If they
are equally good, say tie. Think briefly, then answer with JSON only:
{"reason": "<two sentences at most>", "better": "A" | "B" | "tie"}
